course_details.description: "The field of Entrepreneurship is increasingly important for India as evidenced by policy push for universities as also other sections of the society through the Startup India initiative. Popular research has identified that among various reasons for failure of new ventures, incorrect identification of customer need and problem statement is by far the most prevalent. This course will aid aspiring entrepreneurs (typically B Tech / MTech /PhD students) in deep understanding of customer needs and pain points thus eliminating the waste that occurs. For doctoral students, ethnographic enquiry is a well established methodology for theory building endeavours. With the field of entrepreneurship veering towards 302221entrepreneurship as practice302222 , a sociological approach to understanding this domain, field immersion techniques become crucial from academic research perspective. This methodology which forms the bedrock of theory building is particularly important at the time that India specific theories in the field of entrepreneurship are being sought to better promote new ventures in the economy.""1) Ethnography as a methodology for Innovation & entrepreneurship practice and research2) Gaining access to the field and ethics of ethnographic inquiry3) Participant and Non participant observations4) Forms of data - Visual data, historical data, videos and articles5) Data Collection - conducting Ethnographic interviews, shadowing the protagonists, artefacts6) Data Storage and organization7) Field notes and thick description8) Open and Axial Coding"

course_details.description: "The aim of the course is to expose students to social enterprise and inclusive business and provide an introduction to the concepts, theory and practice of social entrepreneurship, social innovation and social impact and give students a sense of what these different ideas and concepts mean, how they are put into practice, and how they create social value in society. By doing this course, students will gain a deeper appreciation of social innovation, social entrepreneurship, inclusive business practices as well as more conventional business activities to create social impact, such as CSR & ESG, and a better understanding of the discourses and debates around these topics. Students learn about different kinds of social enterprises, using case studies, and look at how business are increasingly focused on social and sustainable business models. An additional aim is to make students excited about social innovation, social entrepreneurship and inclusive business practices, and get them to think about how they may wish to apply some of these ideas in their ventures. Learning outcomes include understanding different types of social enterprises, being able to critically assess them and understand how they are different from regular startups and businesses, becoming aware of how and why working with low-income consumers and beneficiaries can be challenging, and how to adapt. These learning outcomes will be achieved with a mixture of lectures, case study discussions, group exercises, and course project work, and assessed through assignments, and exams.succeed. course_details.description: Many of India`s most successful entrepreneurial companies have been substantially influenced by Angels in the early stage and professionally managed venture capital subsequently for growth. This relationship is examined from both the entrepreneur`s and the venture capitalist`s perspective. From the point of view of the entrepreneur, the course considers how significant business opportunities are identified, planned, and built into sustainable companies; how resources are matched with opportunity; and how, within this framework, founders seek capital and partner with Angels / venture capitalists for value creation . From the point of view of the venture capitalist, the course considers how potential entrepreneurial investments are evaluated, valued, structured, and incentivised for; how different venture capital strategies are deployed; and how venture capitalists raise and manage their own funds. The course includes a term-long project where students work in teams (4-5 students per team) to assess and structure a multi stage funding plan that meets both founder and Venture Capitalists goals.
